objections.claim: Provisioning dedicated Memorystore for Redis instances as a look-aside cache and 24-hour idempotency store incurs continuous non-scaling baseline fees that contradict the diurnal scale-to-zero model and exhaust the €45/store/month budget envelope.
objections.failure_scenario: Memorystore for Redis does not scale to zero; it charges 24/7/365 hourly instance rates based on provisioned RAM tier. Sizing a Memorystore Standard Tier (High Availability with primary and replica across zones to meet 99.95% SLO) or Redis Cluster to absorb 15,000 events/second POS bursts and maintain a 24-hour retention window for millions of idempotency keys requires at least an M2 (5 GB) or M3 tier. A regional HA Redis instance costs between €150 and €300+ per month. During closed store hours (00:00 to 05:00) when Cloud Run scales to zero, Memorystore remains fully provisioned and idle, accumulating 150 hours of wasted capacity per month. If Redis is deployed per store or partitioned into regional clusters, this single non-serverless component breaches the entire €45/store/month cloud compute ceiling regardless of actual scan traffic.
objections.recommended_mitigation: Eliminate dedicated Memorystore Redis from the primary architecture. For read-heavy barcode lookups (15k-60k SKUs per store), utilize PostgreSQL indexed lookups with warm shared buffers, connection pooling, and in-process local LRU caching in Cloud Run instances (3-5 second TTL). For transaction deduplication, enforce idempotency keys directly in PostgreSQL using a dedicated indexed table with automated rolling partition drops via `pg_partman`. If an external cache is deemed mandatory, utilize a multi-tenant shared serverless caching tier or Redis instance pooled across all 1,200 stores (~€0.15/store/month allocation) rather than dedicated provisioned instances.

objections.claim: Mandating Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus Edition with Regional HA (multi-zone standby) creates an irreducible compute cost floor that contradicts the €45/store/month budget and runs with excessive idle capacity during off-peak periods.
objections.failure_scenario: Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus Edition with Regional HA provisions two full-capacity database VMs (primary plus synchronous standby across availability zones) running 24/7 with a 30% Enterprise Plus licensing premium, Data Cache RAM, and provisioned high-performance SSD storage. Even a minimal production-grade instance (db-custom-2-8 Enterprise Plus Regional HA) costs upwards of €400 to €550 per month. If sized to withstand peak Saturday surges (15,000 POS events/sec across 1,200 stores), compute capacity must be over-provisioned to 16+ vCPUs (€2,000–€3,500/month). Because Cloud SQL cannot pause or scale compute down dynamically during off-peak morning hours (05:00-08:00) and nighttime closures (00:00-05:00), the database runs at <3% CPU utilization for over 18 hours per day, wasting thousands of euros per month in idle compute.
objections.recommended_mitigation: Downgrade from Enterprise Plus to standard Cloud SQL Enterprise Edition, rightsizing the primary instance for average daytime load with automated storage increases. Decouple reporting queries onto ephemeral read replicas that are spun up via Cloud Scheduler and Terraform only during peak weekend hours, or offload heavy analytical reads to BigQuery. Clarify the multi-tenancy model to guarantee that a pooled, multi-store Cloud SQL cluster serves hundreds of stores simultaneously, reducing the per-store database infrastructure cost allocation to <€3/store/month.

objections.claim: Decomposing store operations into three discrete Cloud Run services combined with `min-instances=2` creates 6 persistently running container instances with always-allocated CPU, negating serverless scale-to-zero cost savings.
objections.failure_scenario: To mitigate cold-start latency spikes (300-800ms) and satisfy the P95 < 120ms SLA, ADR-0001 specifies `min-instances=2` during store operational hours (05:00–23:00, 18 hours/day). Decomposing the system into three autonomous Cloud Run services (`inbound_dock`, `stock_ledger`, `markdown_engine`) requires running a minimum of 6 container instances continuously. To prevent CPU throttling on background handlers and keep database connection pools warm, these instances must use the 'CPU always allocated' billing model. This generates 108 continuous instance-hours daily per regional deployment. During operational lulls (such as 14:00-16:00 when dock receiving and price markdowns are dormant), 4 of the 6 running instances sit 100% idle while billing full compute charges, inflating serverless baseline costs by 300%.
objections.recommended_mitigation: Consolidate the three microservices into a single modular Cloud Run deployment containing `inbound_dock`, `stock_ledger`, and `markdown_engine` packages behind unified routing. Configure `min-instances=1` (scaling to 2 only during known morning replenishment rushes) with high concurrency (`concurrency=80`). This reduces daytime idle container-hours from 108 to 18–36 hours/day (a 66%–83% reduction in baseline serverless spend) while sharing warm database connection pools and memory caches across all three domains.

objections.claim: Publishing unbatched, fine-grained POS transaction and scan events directly to Cloud Pub/Sub and individual Cloud Tasks triggers runaway 1 KiB minimum billing penalties and excessive task invocation fees at 15,000 events/second.
objections.failure_scenario: During Saturday peak shopping rushes, POS checkout registers and mobile scanners generate 15,000 events per second across 1,200 stores. Each transaction line item (averaging 250–350 bytes of JSON) is published as an individual Pub/Sub message. Google Cloud Pub/Sub enforces a minimum 1 KiB billing quota per message. As a result, Carrefour is billed for 15,000 KiB/sec (~14.6 MiB/sec or ~1.3 TB/day of billed ingestion) instead of the actual ~350 GB transmitted, quadrupling ingestion billing. Furthermore, dispatching downstream ERP synchronization via individual Cloud Tasks at $0.40 per million tasks generates 54 million task operations per hour ($21.60/hour, accumulating over $15,000/month during peak periods). When Pub/Sub push subscriptions invoke Cloud Run endpoints on every discrete message, 15,000 HTTP POST calls per second trigger extreme container autoscaling churn and millions of billable Cloud Run invocations.
objections.recommended_mitigation: Implement client-side or edge-gateway micro-batching. Store POS edge concentrators and handheld devices must buffer stock movements and basket depletions into batches of 50–100 items (or within a 250ms sliding window) before publishing a single multi-record envelope to Pub/Sub, maximizing the 1 KiB billing boundary and slashing message volume by up to 90%. Replace discrete Cloud Tasks per item with batched background reconciliation jobs, and configure Pub/Sub push subscriptions with batch delivery settings (`max_messages=100`, `max_delay=1s`) to minimize Cloud Run invocation fees.

objections.claim: Direct ad-hoc querying of BigQuery audit and shrinkage logs by store and department dashboards without enforced partitioning and clustering causes full-table scans that lead to catastrophic on-demand analytical costs.
objections.failure_scenario: Architecture Section 1.2 and PRD FR-5.3 specify that stock movements, dual-key shrinkage approvals, and POS depletions stream into BigQuery to power real-time shrinkage heatmaps, cycle counts, and AGEC tax reports. At 15,000 events/sec, BigQuery ingests over 1.3 billion records (~2 TB) monthly. When 1,200 store directors and department managers open their web consoles daily to query shrinkage patterns by aisle or category, unpartitioned and unclustered ad-hoc SQL queries execute full-table scans across the entire multi-terabyte dataset. At $6.25 per TB on-demand analysis pricing, 2,400 daily dashboard refreshes scanning 2 TB per query would bill 4.8 PB of scan data daily ($30,000/day in BigQuery analysis charges), instantly exceeding the annual IT budget in days.
objections.recommended_mitigation: Enforce strict table partitioning on `DATE(event_timestamp)` and clustering on `(store_id, department_id, aisle_id)` for all BigQuery audit and shrinkage tables. Enforce maximum billing quotas (`maximum_bytes_billed`) on dashboard service accounts to reject runaway queries. To completely avoid scanning raw analytical tables from operational dashboards, deploy pre-aggregated materialized views (e.g. hourly shrinkage rollup tables per store) or route interactive dashboard queries to a PostgreSQL read replica, restricting BigQuery to scheduled nighttime carbon-aware batch reports.

objections.claim: Using legacy Serverless VPC Access connectors combined with cross-zone regional HA replication and cross-region backups creates hidden networking egress traps and idle VM costs.
objections.failure_scenario: Architecture Section 5.1 specifies Serverless VPC Access connectors to bridge Cloud Run with private Cloud SQL and Memorystore Redis instances. Standard Serverless VPC connectors require dedicated VM instances (minimum 2–3 `f1-micro` or `e2-micro` instances running 24/7). Provisioning connectors across three Cloud Run microservices incurs continuous baseline compute charges of €60–€90/month just for idle connector routing. Furthermore, Serverless VPC Access bills $0.01 per GB for connector egress. At 15,000 requests/sec, connector data egress reaches tens of terabytes monthly. Additionally, replicating Cloud SQL transactions synchronously across zones in `europe-west9` and streaming backups to `europe-west1` (Belgium) incurs inter-zone ($0.01/GB) and inter-region ($0.02/GB) network egress fees, compounding hidden monthly network bills that are excluded from the compute budget calculation.
objections.recommended_mitigation: Replace Serverless VPC Access connectors with Google Cloud Run Direct VPC Egress, which attaches container instances directly to the VPC subnet without intermediary connector VMs, completely eliminating idle connector VM charges and connector throughput surcharges. Keep transactional read-paths within local container memory caches to minimize inter-zone traffic, and compress/deduplicate all cross-region database backups to `europe-west1` to minimize inter-region network egress.
